messages.author: f00aa06a56a6d110
messages.subject: longitudinal EFA and CFA
parts:
Hi all

I'm working on a longitudinal framework with an unbalanced  panel of three years. I'm constructing a new measure and I want to identify the number of dimensions underlying the new developed instrument.

Please I have a question about running factor analysis for longitudinal data using lavaan. Is it possible to use one time point to run EFA and two time-points  to run CFA. I think about this approach beacause my sapmle size is small (62 firms for the first year, 74 for the second year and 70 for the third year)
 so I can't split it to cross-validate the model suggested by EFA and even if I split the data in each time point , the models suggested are not equivalent in the sense that items load differently in factors at each year leading to uncertainty about the best model to submit to confirmatory analysis.

Thanks in advance for your precious support!!
Lina.

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: longitudinal EFA and CFA
parts: Is it possible to use one time point to run EFA and two time-points  to run CFA. I think about this approach beacause my sapmle size is small (62 firms for the first year, 74 for the second year and 70 for the third year)

That's a really small sample size, so I would trust EFA results unless you have like 10 highly reliable indicators for each supposed factor.  But it sounds like you already have ideas about how items load on factors at each timepoint, so I don't understand why you would be motivated to run EFA at all.

This isn't anything specific to lavaan, so SEMNET is a better place to get feedback on this problem.

Terry
